title: The first word: recite
translation: Recite in the name of your Lord who created, created the human being from a clinging clot. Recite! Your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught the human being what he did not know.
body: **Nöldeke** and most Muslim tradition (Aisha's report in al-Bukhari) treat these verses as the first revelation, around 610; a minority named Surah 74 instead. **Iqraʾ** shares its root with **Qurʾān**, which some Western scholars derive from Syriac qeryānā, “scripture reading”. Most Muslim authorities trace it directly to Arabic qaraʾa.
question: Does iqraʾ sound to you more like “read”, “recite”, or “proclaim”? What in verses 1–5 points your way?
source_label: Nöldeke, Geschichte des Qorāns · etymology of Qurʾān
reading: Nicolai Sinai, The Qur'an: A Historical-Critical Introduction (2017)
